title: Life events
hookLine: new jobs, new babies, moves: practice bends, doesn't break
tomorrow: did the Buddha ever need a doctor?

cards: A first job rearranges a whole morning. Mai starts at a bakery this Saturday: an alarm before sunrise, flour on her sleeves, and her morning sit squeezed down to almost nothing.
Her messages this week are half pride, half panic. New jobs, new babies, moves, a parent's new shift: life keeps rearranging the hours, and a practice has to find new ones or quietly disappear.
Near the end of his life, the Buddha's own routine broke too.

teach.h: ALONE FOR THE RAINS AT BELUVA.
teach.b: The Digha Nikaya tells of the rains at Beluva. He sends the monks off to spend the season with friends around Vesali, and stays on alone. Then a serious illness comes, with sharp pains, and he bears it, mindful and clear.

teach.h: A WORN-OUT CART, HELD WITH STRAPS.
teach.b: Afterward he tells Ananda that his body is like a worn-out cart, kept going only with straps. And then he keeps walking, and keeps teaching, on a slower road.
That's the teaching under today's line: practice bends with a life. Lay Buddhists fit it around work and family: a few breaths before a shift, a chant on the bus, the precepts kept at the counter.
Shorter isn't failure. Stopping completely is where it can break.

teach.h: SIX LINES FOR A BUSY WEEK.
teach.b: And this week's carries all still fit in a busy day. Assaji's walk: by example. Brahma's request: only when asked.
Rahula's mirror: one breath for a child. The farmer: keep sitting.
The Kalamas: doubt, honestly. Dhammadinna: look at it. Six lines, and every one of them fits in a bakery apron.

how: Lay Buddhists fit practice around work and family, shortening a sit, chanting on a commute or keeping the precepts at work when life changes, rather than stopping altogether.

where he stayed alone for the rains

s: the Buddha's own routine never changed
at Beluva he sent the monks away for the rains and fell seriously ill. he kept going, differently.
a shorter practice doesn't really count
the old cart kept moving with straps. shorter isn't stopping.
Dhammadinna taught that a neutral feeling is pleasant when it's known

games.q: your neighbor just had a baby and says her quiet morning practice is 'gone for a year.' what fits today's line?
o: she's right: pause it all and restart when life calms down.
find a smaller form, like a few breaths while the baby sleeps.
keep the full practice by sleeping less.
games.why: bend, don't break: the Buddha kept walking and teaching on a worn-out cart. a smaller form keeps the thread.

practice: Make a tiny plan. Pick the busiest day of your coming week and find one spot in it, the bus, a doorway, the minute before work starts, where three breaths could fit. See yourself taking them there.
Then use the sit to take three now, slowly, as a rehearsal, and rest.

wordCard.voice: Life events: new jobs, new babies, moves. The Buddha's old cart kept rolling with straps, and a practice can too.

carryVoice: Bend, don't break: a shorter sit is still a sit, even in a bakery apron. That's the week.

sources.ref: Digha Nikaya 16 (Mahaparinibbana Sutta, chapter 2: the rains at Beluva, the illness, the worn-out cart)
